text:
maya_support: Hey team — customer reported recurring tail latency spikes on the embeddings route this morning. spikes ~1.5–3s, baseline ~120ms. also saw a few 422s with "dimension mismatch" during the same window. repro attached.

kevin_cs: Thanks Maya. Customer is ACME. They said it started after they increased max_batch_size to 256 in their route config. previously 64.

maya_support: Exact quote from customer: "we pushed max_batch_size to 256 to improve throughput and now small requests sometimes hang while a single large request runs, leading to tail p99 jumps."

henry_runtime: can you paste their route config and a minimal repro? need to know coalesce window and dynamic batching flags.

maya_support: Pasting their route snippet (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "embed-3b",
  "batching": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_batch_size": 256,
    "dynamic": true,
    "coalesce_ms": 50
  }
}
```

leila_ml: 50ms coalesce with 256 max_batch_size seems aggressive for mixed-size workload. Small requests will wait to fill big batches. Could be starvation on small reqs.

sam_infra: Ops metrics from the time window (summarized): queue depth peaked at 420, concurrent batches avg jumped from 8->26, GPU utilization steady, but KV cache miss rate increased ~3x.

maya_support: Customer also sent a curl that produced a 422 intermittently: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-3b","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```
Response snippet: 
```json
{ "error": "Unprocessable Entity", "message": "embedding dimension 1536 does not match model dimension 2048" }
```

henry_runtime: Dimension mismatch is odd — suggests mixed model variants being routed or an older quantized variant with different output dim. But that shouldn't cause latency spikes. Separate issue but could be fallout from fallback routing.

leila_ml: Two hypotheses: 1) Large batched requests (many vectors) fill up slots causing small ones to wait (tail spike). 2) Some requests routed to a variant with different embedding dims causing 422s and triggering retries, which then increase queue pressure.

kevin_cs: Customer says they saw p99 go from 0.15s to ~2.8s after a release where they bumped max_batch_size + enabled dynamic. They reverted config to 64 and p99 improved.

henry_runtime: Helpful repro idea: run an interleaved workload locally: mix many 1-item requests with occasional 1000-item requests and compare p99 with max_batch_size 64 vs 256. @kevin_cs can you ask ACME to run this or provide trace logs?

kevin_cs: I got a mini trace from their SDK with requestIDs. Pasting trimmed logs:
```
[2025-06-01T10:02:13Z] recv req 0xabc size=1 route=embed-3b
[2025-06-01T10:02:13Z] recv req 0xabd size=1000 route=embed-3b
[2025-06-01T10:02:13Z] batch create id=0 slots=1000 scheduled
[2025-06-01T10:02:13Z] batch create id=1 slots=1 scheduled
[2025-06-01T10:02:13Z] batch 0 running duration=1.9s
[2025-06-01T10:02:14Z] batch 1 waiting for GPU slot (blocked by batch 0)
[2025-06-01T10:02:15Z] batch 1 executed duration=0.11s
```

sam_infra: That log aligns with a single large batch occupying GPU for ~1.9s while small batches wait — exactly tail spike behavior.

henry_runtime: Root cause: oversized max_batch_size coupled with static slot allocation leads to head-of-line blocking for small requests. Dynamic batching should mitigate by prioritizing small requests or preempting, but their config probably didn't enable small-request preemption.

maya_support: What immediate mitigation can we recommend to ACME while we investigate?

henry_runtime: Short-term options:
- Set max_batch_size back to 64 (they already tested this).
- Reduce coalesce_ms to 10–20ms to avoid waiting too long for large fills.
- Enable small_request_preempt=true (if on their plan) or set priority tags on small requests.

leila_ml: Also check routing policies: pin heavy bulk ingestion clients to a dedicated pool or use a dedicated capacity queue. That prevents interleaving with low-latency interactive traffic.

kevin_cs: I'll relay recommendations. They asked for a more permanent fix on our side.

henry_runtime: Long-term runtime fixes: implement preemptible slots (allow small priority batches to preempt long-running large batches), or add an adaptive slotting algorithm that splits huge batches across multiple micro-batches so single large requests don't monopolize the GPU for multiple seconds. We've prototyped micro-batching before.

sam_infra: Filed infra ticket RINF-8274 to evaluate adaptive slotting and priority preemption. Linking in this thread.

ops-bot: Incident RINF-8274 created by sam_infra (priority P2). https://redwood.internal/ops/RINF-8274

kevin_cs: Customer happy with immediate recommendations, will try coalesce=20 and max_batch_size=64 first. Also asked if we can add a server-side guard that warns when user sets max_batch_size > 128 on mixed-size routes.

henry_runtime: We can add a validation warning in the console/API that suggests lower max_batch_size for routes with mixed-size distribution. Filing a small docs/config UX ticket.

leila_ml: For the 422 dimension errors — ask customer to ensure they aren't mixing model variants. We'll add an alert if fallback to a variant with differing dims occurs.

maya_support: Thanks all. kevin, please post customer's follow-up once they test config changes. I'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
